guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.title: Add Text to Wedding Photos: Legibility Rules
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.desc: Place names, dates and quotes on wedding photos so they stay readable in print and on small screens, with contrast and safe-margin guidance.
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.lead: Text over a photograph needs a quiet area to sit on. If you have to add a heavy shadow to make it readable, the crop is wrong.
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.f1v: Aim for strong light/dark separation behind the lettering
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.f2v: Keep text at least 5% in from every edge
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.f3v: Check legibility at thumbnail size, not just full screen
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.f4v: Two typefaces at most; confirm the licence for print
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.s1: Look for negative space — sky, a plain wall, an out-of-focus background — and place the text there rather than over faces. Limit yourself to one hierarchy: a headline and a smaller line for the date. Then view the image at 25% zoom or on a phone; if the small line disappears, increase the size contrast or drop it.
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.s2: US save-the-dates and invitations commonly use the full date spelled out, while UK and European stationery often use day-month-year ordering, so '03/04/2027' means different things to different guests. Spell the month to remove ambiguity. For bilingual families, check that the chosen font supports both scripts and that a longer translation does not overflow the safe margin — German and Russian text can run 30% longer than English.
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.s3: Do not place text across a high-detail area, and do not rely on a drop shadow as your only contrast fix. Avoid very thin type weights, which disappear after social-platform compression. Before printing, confirm the font is licensed for commercial print and convert text to outlines or embed it in the exported PDF.
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.q1: Where should text go on a wedding photo?
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.a1: In an area of low detail with good contrast, at least 5% in from every edge, and never across a face or the main subject.
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.q2: How do I keep text readable on a busy background?
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.a2: Add a subtle gradient or a semi-transparent panel behind the text, or recrop to find negative space. A heavy drop shadow usually looks worse.
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.q3: Should I write the date with numbers?
guides.add-text-to-wedding-photo.a3: Spell out the month. Numeric dates are read differently in the US and Europe and cause real confusion for international guests.
